title: Baratunde Thurston, a fellow Masters of Scale speaker, picks Eric as his favorite — 'Seeing someone own their role in the current collapse and try to make it right was hella inspiring'
summary: Thurston was not in the audience — he hosted Danny Meyer's session and appeared with Bob Safian — and his write-up of the summit runs through Meredith Whittaker, Meyer and the theme of agency before it reaches Eric. What he singles out is not the argument but the posture: that the man whose first book shaped how a generation of founders build said so plainly, named the financial gravity pulling companies from their purpose, and set about repairing it. In his account Eric reminded the room that companies once lost their charters for behavior now treated as normal.
blockquote: Watching someone that influential tell a more interdependent story was a gift. Seeing someone own their role in the current collapse and try to make it right was shocking tbh, and hella inspiring.
